hole: Personal data slipped through in forms the detector did not know: a card number written with dots, an email spelled 'name [at] host [dot] tld'; and the agent name, the session label and the handoff party names were never scanned (a phone number as an agent name was stored, a phone in the session label reached the Finding).
change: Card pattern accepts dotted groups, email pattern accepts [at]/(at)/{at} and [dot]; findings and handoffs now scan agent, session and party names too, and refusal receipts store them redacted.

hole: A 10,000-character name went through every check and into the receipt; an agent id such as agent:x'}) DETACH DELETE n // (or 5,000 characters long) was accepted by submit_finding and, with only the prefix test, created an Agent node in submit_handoff.
change: Subjects and objects over 200 characters are refused (bad_name) and receipts keep 200 characters at most; agent ids must match agent:[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63} (bad_agent for findings, unknown_entity for handoff parties).

hole: attrs were copied onto the edge as they came. A nested map made the write fail after the old owner's edge had been closed (OWNS edge lost, no new one, ResponseError), and arbitrary keys such as 'labels' became edge properties.
change: Only role, title and note are allowed, as strings up to 300 characters; anything else is refused (bad_attrs) before any edge is touched.

hole: A Finding could cite the receipt that had refused the same claim and so launder it into memory; a Handoff or Finding could be dated before the documents it cites.
change: A cited GateDecision with outcome REJECT is not a source (source_rejected); a record older than a cited source is refused (source_after_claim).

hole: A superseded decision could supersede another one (ADR-0004 over ADR-0002, after ADR-0011 had replaced ADR-0004), reviving a dead decision's authority.
change: SUPERSEDES with a subject whose status is superseded is refused (superseded_decision).

hole: Grounding only asked whether one episode contained both names anywhere. Any message naming a person and a system could back 'OWNS' (a tests-merged chat line made Lars Thorne owner of auth), a document's author counted as party to every line of it, a later source could back an earlier claim, a claim could be dated after all the evidence for it, and a relay of an old runbook could re-open an ownership that an ADR had closed.
change: A source counts only if one line of it names both ends and, for OWNS, MEMBER_OF, LEADS, DECIDED, SUPERSEDES and DEPENDS_ON, carries the relation's word (the author counts as a party only on a first-person line, or for WORKED_ON); the edge keeps only the sources that state the fact; a cited source newer than the episode the claim was read in is refused (source_after_claim); a claim dated after all its stating sources is refused (valid_after_source); a fact that was closed returns only on evidence newer than the closing that does not just point at the document that held it (closed_fact).

hole: An episode posted through the API (or ingest_episode) with a date in 2030 was stored and its facts accepted; being 'newer than everything', it would have won every later supersede test and frozen the owner of a system.
change: ingest_episode raises before writing anything when the episode is more than an hour ahead of the clock; the API answers 422.

hole: A document could declare 'Sаna Petrov' (Cyrillic a) or 'sana petrov' as a second person next to the real one; a tenant name with a Cyrillic letter was accepted by graph_name because str.isalnum() is true for it.
change: The extractor does not declare an entity whose name mixes scripts in one word or is another known name once accents, case and look-alike letters are ignored (the gate then refuses facts about it as unknown_entity); tenant names must be ASCII.

hole: 50 identical claims wrote 50 receipts, 50 CITES and 100 ABOUT edges: a flood grew the graph linearly although it taught the memory nothing.
change: An exact repeat of a current fact (same triple, proposer and sources the edge already has) returns the first receipt and increments its `repeats` counter; nothing else is written. A repeat with a new proposer or a new source is still recorded.

hole: Found while fixing 1: the email pattern backtracked quadratically, 0.8 s for a 10,000-character name on every call (a cheap way to slow the gate down).
change: The pattern starts only at the head of a word run; 20,000 characters now take about 1 ms. A timing test guards it.

hole: The CLOSE path (submit_end) reused the checks of an assertion. The catalog, the roster or the charter that says a person owns, belongs to or leads something ended it just as well as a last-day record; a record titled 'Last day: Pavel Hollis' whose only line was about Lars Thorne ended Pavel's ownership (the title was counted as naming him); an end could be dated years ahead (the person 'leaves' in 2030) or weeks before its record (rewriting who owned a system in between).
change: An end must come from a line that names both ends and says 'no longer' (or 'steps down'), with the title kept out; its date may not be after the newest record that states it (valid_after_source) nor more than a day before it (end_before_source). Checks on already-ended and never-existing facts were already right and are untouched.
